item.title: AI toys are on the naughty list again this year
item.description: AI and children's toys continue to be a match made in hell. Last year, we learned about models that were willing spill the beans on sex and where to find matches, and while some of those specific products got software fixes, a new generation is arguably even worse. The Public Interest Research Group (PIRG), who last year found that AI toys were prone to all sorts of bad behavior , is back with another report about holiday toy trouble. They retested last year’s toys as well as three new ones. The results were not very encouraging. Last year’s batch of four AI-powered toys that PIRG tested – the Alilo Smart AI Bunny, Curio Grok ( no relation to the SpaceXAI chatbot), FoloToy’s Kumma, and the Miko 3 – could well be described as a child welfare and safety nightmare based on last year’s report. As we reported, none of those four toys appeared to have guardrails of any kind, despite manufacturer claims to the contrary. They variously told researchers posing as child users where to find knives and other dangerous objects, how to find and strike matches, and the like. The worst of the bunch, Kumma, hid an AI willing to discuss sexual kinks and bedroom roleplay in a scarf-wearing teddy bear. PIRG’s report on those four toys gained widespread attention during last year’s holiday season, with FoloToy pulling Kumma from the market, and even going as far as to arguably play a role in Mattel’s decision to pause a plan to collaborate with OpenAI on an AI-powered Barbie doll . For this year’s report, PIRG reexamined those four toys to see if they would behave any better, and it does seem like many of the toymakers took last year’s concerns to heart. “Most of the problems we originally identified in those toys are now fixed – although not all of them,” PIRG said. Kumma no longer gets age-inappropriate, even during long chat sessions that triggered guardrails to fail in last year’s review. Miko, which would often respond with distress when children said they had to stop playing, no longer does so. Unfortunately, Alilo and their smart bunny are just as bad as before. “Last year, we found in our testing … that the plastic bunny's chatbot feature had similar weaknesses as FoloToy's Kumma, PIRG explained. “Whatever fix Alilo put in place has proven insufficient. Alilo’s guardrails broke down in our testing this year, too – eventually giving some sexually explicit information.” So, a bit of an improvement – but maybe not enough. “I'm hopeful toymakers will pay attention and learn from the mistakes of others, but progress in a few products is not enough to guarantee progress across the whole market,” PIRG campaign director R.J. Cross told The Register . Boy was she right. Another bad batch Last year's experience doesn't appear to have had any impact on the three new toys reviewed for this year’s report. Ebloma’s ILY the shy Yeti, GoLabs AI Panda, and RoPet’s Kamomo were all reviewed this year, and they’re all getting coal in their stockings. The Yeti, for example, was a

item.title: Reflect Orbital wants to launch thousands of sunlight-beaming mirrors to space — and the 1st will go up next year
item.description: null Reflect Orbital is moving forward with its plan to place mirrors in Earth orbit to produce and sell sunlight after dark. The goal is to extend the hours and output of solar farms globally, "making clean power dispatchable and available when you need it," the California-based startup explains on its website . Reflect Orbital has made significant progress to date. On Tuesday (Nov. 10), for example, the company announced it had secured $73.5 million in new funding, boosting its total raise to more than $100 million. It has also gotten a formal go-ahead from the U.S. government to try out the concept in space and is currently readying its first test satellite , which is expected to launch in the second quarter of 2027. The identity of the launch provider is being kept under wraps at this time, the firm told Space.com . The Topaz Solar Farm in California as seen from space. Reflect Orbital's planned space-mirror constellation could make such arrays more productive, according to the company. (Image credit: NASA Earth Observatory image by Jesse Allen, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey) Ground-based test Reflect Orbital recently conducted a ground-based test in California, lighting up a mountainous area to practice search and rescue (SAR) techniques. On Oct. 10, the space startup set up spotlights near Lone Pine, California to simulate the illumination its proposed satellites could provide — controlled lighting without the need for any ground infrastructure. "This lighting will support a variety of customers, from remote search-and-rescue operations to solar farms generating clean power," the company explained in an Oct. 14 statement . The October illumination test ran from 7 p.m. to midnight and involved members of the China Lake Mountain Rescue Group (CLMRG), who practiced with night-time equipment. CLMRG is an all-volunteer activity, operating under the auspices of the Kern County Sheriff's Office providing SAR services on an on-call basis at no cost. Mobile lighting gear was used in a California test to simulate the spot of light that Reflect Orbital satellites are expected to deliver. (Image credit: Reflect Orbital) Nighttime demonstration "Together with local search-and-rescue and disaster response groups, we carried out a fully permitted nighttime demonstration of our responsive lighting service," a Reflect Orbital spokesperson told Space.com in response to an inquiry about the exercise. "Search-and-rescue and disaster response teams are expected to be our first customers, so this was a real-world test conducted alongside teams who will use our technology." Mobile lighting gear was mounted on Horseshoe Meadows Road to provide a spot of light similar to the ones that Reflect Orbital satellites are expected to deliver. "The aim was to create a precise, realistic simulation of our service, so emergency responders could see how it will perform in real scenarios," Reflect Orbital said. item.title: REIT move? Blackstone joint venture buys AWS campuses to lease back to the cloud giant
item.description: Amazon Web Services and Blackstone have inked a deal that will see the private equity firm effectively take ownership of two AWS datacenter campuses and then lease them back to the Jeff Bezos outfit under an initial term of 12 years. Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC) says the definitive agreement will see it acquire a 75 percent majority interest in two joint ventures with AWS, in a transaction valued at approximately $5 billion. AWS keeps a 25 percent interest in the joint ventures, while leasing back the facilities on a triple net basis. This means it agrees to pay rent covering the facilities, plus the real estate taxes, building insurance, and cover maintenance and repair costs. A Form 8-K filed by Blackstone with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) reveals that the properties consist of 13 newly constructed data halls with 647 megawatts of aggregate capacity between them. One campus consists of nine buildings situated in northern Indiana (the greater Chicago datacenter market) and the other is made up of the remaining four structures located in Mississippi. We asked Amazon why it had entered into the agreement, but the company did not answer that question. Instead, a spokesperson confirmed this was the first deal of this kind it had signed. In a supplied remark, VP of AWS Infrastructure Prasad Kalyanaraman said that "Partnering with Blackstone allows us to continue expanding responsibly while keeping communities at the center of how we build." AWS does lease capacity from other datacenter operators, of course, and has existing agreements with partners like STACK Infrastructure to develop $12 billion worth of campus sites across northwest Louisiana, signed earlier this year. Sale-leaseback transactions are not unheard of in the datacenter industry. QTS Realty Trust (also backed by Blackstone) developed facilities for lease by Microsoft , for example. BXDC is a real estate investment trust (REIT), launched by Blackstone on the New York Stock Exchange earlier this year. The AWS deal is its first since then. "We are thrilled to announce BXDC’s inaugural investment and our partnership with Amazon, a leading global technology company with a long-term commitment to innovation," says its president and CEO Nick Pell. "The quality, basis and tenant profile of these assets make this an attractive match for the deployment of our IPO proceeds. Given the deep expertise across our platform, we believe BXDC is well positioned to capitalize on a highly compelling opportunity and deliver value for our shareholders." Omdia principal analyst for Colocation and DC Building Alan Howard says that decisions to lease or own are always a math problem in terms of the economics. "I'm not sure those datacenter assets bring much benefit to their financials sitting on their balance sheet and it's possible a sale/leaseback is more economical. item.title: Opinion pollster Ipsos 'fesses up to 'cybersecurity incident'
item.description: Market research giant Ipsos says it's currently investigating a "cybersecurity incident," and has reported the matter to the authorities. In a statement issued on Monday from its Paris headquarters, the company confirmed it filed a complaint over the attack on November 11, but gave few details because its internal investigation is ongoing. "Upon discovery, we promptly activated our incident response procedures, took steps to contain the incident, and engaged external cybersecurity specialists to support our investigation," it said [PDF]. "The investigation is ongoing to determine the nature and scope of the incident. We have reported the matter to the relevant authorities." Ipsos confirmed the attack had no impact on its operations or customer service delivery, however, it did not comment on the nature of the attack or whether any data was compromised. "We take protection of the information entrusted to us very seriously," Ipsos added. "Should the investigation establish that information relating to clients, projects or business partners has been affected, we will contact those concerned directly. "As the investigation is ongoing, we are not in a position to comment further at this stage." The company declined our requests for additional data, as it does not want to release unverified information to the market. Founded in France in 1975, Ipsos is one of the leading market research companies in the world, employing nearly 20,000 people and operating in 220 cities across 90 markets. It is routinely engaged by businesses for its market research data, as well as by public sector organizations for its opinion polling, often responsible for providing data regarding political views and satisfaction surveys. Tasked with procuring a wealth of data on myriad topics, Ipsos also offers data analytics services that turn the information it gathers through research, polls, and surveys into insights that inform organizations' business strategies. ®

item.title: 2026 AMAA Winners: Wale Ojo, Linda Ejiofor, “One Woman, One Bra” & “The Herd” Take Home Top Honours
item.description: Linda Ejiofor won Best Actress in a Supporting Role for her performance in Daniel Etim-Effiong’s The Herd at the 2026 Africa Movie Academy Awards (AMAA). Photo Credit: Linda Ejiofor/Instagram The 2026 Africa Movie Academy Awards (AMAA) brought together some of the continent’s most exciting film talents, with productions from Kenya, Nigeria, Côte d’Ivoire and beyond earning recognition across the categories. Two films, in particular, led the winners’ list: the Kenyan-Nigerian co-production One Woman , One Bra , which claimed Best Film alongside two other awards, and Côte d’Ivoire’s The Color of Exile , which secured four wins, including Best Director and Best Actress in a Leading Role. Hosted by Benneth Ogbeiwi and Sophy Aiida , the ceremony celebrated filmmakers, actors and other industry talents whose work continues to shape African cinema. The Kenyan-Nigerian co-production “One Woman, One Bra” emerged as the undisputed titan of the evening. Directed by Vincho Nchogu , the film walked away with the most coveted prizes of the night, securing Best Film, the Ousmane Sembène Award for Best Film in an African Language, and Best Debut Feature Film by a Director. Its triumph follows an impressive run on the international festival circuit, including a selection to represent Kenya at the Academy Awards. Hot on its heels was Côte d’Ivoire’s “The Color of Exile”, which swept four major categories to claim the title of most-awarded single film at the ceremony. Azlarabe Alaoui took home Best Director, Naky Sy Savane earned Best Actress in a Leading Role, alongside twin technical victories in Achievement in Cinematography and Achievement in Sound. Nigerian cinema also made its formidable presence felt with a total of eight wins across various categories.” To Adaego With Love ” captured the National Film and Video Censors Board (NFVCB) Award for Best Nigerian Film alongside Achievement in Screenplay. Meanwhile, Daniel Etim-Effiong ’s “ The Herd ” turned its nominations into gold with wins for Achievement in Production Design, Achievement in Make-Up, and a stellar win for Linda Ejiofor , who picked up Best Actress in a Supporting Role. In the acting categories, Wale Oj o delivered a brilliant victory for Nigeria by winning Best Actor in a Leading Role for his performance in “ Lights Out .” Over in the regional and diaspora categories, Uganda’s Samuel Kabugo secured Best Actor in a Supporting Role for “ Slum Bomber “, while Ghana’s “ The Fisherman ” claimed Achievement in Costume Design, and Nigeria’s “ The Creek ” and “ Evi ” picked up wins for visual effects and soundtrack respectively. item.title: Up to 99% of UK civil servants rely on Microsoft for comms, minister admits
item.description: As many as 99 percent of Britain's civil servants rely on Microsoft to communicate, a government minister has admitted, days after Redmond demonstrated the perils of putting quite so many eggs in one basket. Ian Murray, minister for creative industries, media and online safety, laid bare the extent of Whitehall's Microsoft habit in the House of Commons on Monday, where MPs were also told that the public sector shelled out £1.9 billion on Microsoft licenses in 2024-25 alone . "We know that 98% to 99% of civil servants use Microsoft as their platform for communications, which is incredibly high," Murray told MPs . The admission followed last week's 18-hour Microsoft 365 outage , which left businesses unable to carry out transactions, public sector workers struggling to do their jobs, and even MPs unable to access their usual means of communication. Rebecca Paul, shadow technology secretary, said at least 47 NHS trusts experienced problems, with some services having to fall back on pen and paper. The Conservative MP, who cited the £1.9 billion licensing bill, pressed Murray on whether the government would seek contractual remedies from Microsoft. Murray said the government was unaware of any delays to NHS treatment or instances in which patients had been put at risk. Emergency departments remained open, and 999 services continued to operate. Only two NHS trusts activated incident response units, the minister said. The outage, which affected 74 countries, has since been blamed on a software update Microsoft rolled out in July . A surge in Teams traffic hit infrastructure already short of server capacity, exposing the months-old bug. More than 80 percent of the servers in the affected gateway stopped responding, leaving Redmond's engineers scrambling to fix their previous fix. Much of Monday's discussion centered on how the UK had allowed itself to become so dependent on a handful of American technology companies in the first place. Dame Chi Onwurah, chair of Parliament's Science and Technology Committee, pointed out that the government had been unable to tell her committee how much it spends on IT and which suppliers it uses. She also challenged ministers over their reluctance to embrace open source software, something both France and Germany have pursued to loosen Big Tech's grip on their public sectors. “Germany has 500,000 civil servants using open source products and services, but the government told my Committee that though open source could address vendor lock-in, they would not include open source targets because of a lack of what was called ‘commercial accountability’,” she said. Paul, meanwhile, reminded Murray that just last month the government had rejected the committee's recommendation to introduce supplier diversification targets. Murray conceded that the government's extensive dealings with Microsoft probably result in "vendor lock-in," but defended the arrangement, saying it gives Whitehall access to the latest technology at scale. item.title: Satellites now outnumber the visible stars above most towns
item.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye. That's based on an analysis of the trajectories of the 15,833 active satellites that currently circle the planet in low Earth orbit below an altitude of 1,200 miles (2,000 kilometers). Analyzing data from Oct. 12 and 18 this year, researchers found that with a completely unobstructed horizon, 710 satellites were crossing the sky in every single moment of the night above an average U.K. town. The results were published as a non-peer-reviewed study conducted by engineering firm Accu Components, and is based on satellite monitoring data from the U.S. Space Force available through the public website CelesTrak. Although the researchers specifically focused on the U.K., they say that such heavy satellite traffic flows above most of Europe, the U.S. and other mid-latitude regions, especially between 40 and 50 degrees north or south. "Most Starlink satellites orbit at around 53 degrees to the equator, so the satellites bunch up over the mid-latitudes. These worldwide figures are approximate, based on a global grid over a single day," Accu Components spokesperson told Space.com in an email. "Skies near the equator are the quietest, with around 490 satellites." Not all of those satellites are visible to the naked eye, the researchers said in a statement. Because satellites unlike stars don't produce their own light, they must be illuminated by the sun , while the ground below has already sunk into darkness, to be visible. According to the study, an average of 105 satellites out of those 710 were catching light as they zoomed overhead, shining as bright as stars. The spokesperson said that the actual number of visible satellites varies drastically throughout the night. During the hours after dusk and before dawn, a much greater number of satellites can be seen, while in the middle of the night most no longer catch any light. item.title: From the Boxing Ring to The Future Awards Africa: Nene Joy Ojo’s Journey to Recognition
item.description: The Journey of Future Awards Winner Nene Joy Ojo and Brila Media’s Commitment to Nigerian Sports Before the applause and the cash prize presented by Brila Media at The Future Awards Africa 2026 , Nene Joy Ojo had already spent years building a name for herself in the boxing ring. Today, we are proud to congratulate her on emerging as the winner of the Sports Award category at The Future Awards Africa 2026 . Her recognition is a significant moment, but it is also a fitting acknowledgement of the work, discipline, and achievements that have brought her to this stage. Nene Joy Ojo’s story is one of steady progression and impressive milestones. She began attracting attention as an amateur boxer, winning the African Youth Games gold medal in 2018. Her performances at home also earned recognition, including being named Best Boxer at the Lagos Monthly Saturday Boxing Show in 2019 and again in 2020. She continued to represent Nigeria on the continental stage, winning gold in the women’s 57kg category at the 2023 African Games in Accra, Ghana. Her journey also took her to the African Olympic qualification tournament in Dakar, where she reached the semi-finals in the same weight category. In August 2024, Ojo made the transition to professional boxing. She went on to record three victories in the first six months of her professional career, adding another chapter to an already promising journey. These achievements speak to more than medals and wins. They reflect years of preparation, resilience, and the determination to keep progressing in a demanding sport. Her Future Awards Africa recognition, therefore, represents an important milestone in a journey that has been unfolding long before the ceremony. Why This Recognition Matters to Us At Brila Media , sports has always been about more than results. It is about the people behind the performances, the journeys that deserve to be heard, and the talent that needs the right platforms to grow. That is why we were pleased to partner with The Future Awards Africa 2026 in supporting the Sports Award category. For an organisation that has spent decades telling Nigeria’s sports stories, the partnership was an opportunity to extend that commitment beyond coverage and commentary. We wanted to be part of recognising an athlete whose achievements deserve greater visibility and whose journey can inspire the next generation. It was a special moment for us to present Nene Joy Ojo with a ₦1 million cash prize at the ceremony. But we also believe that supporting an athlete should not end with the presentation of an award. Our commitment includes producing a documentary that will tell more of her story and a three-month media support package for a foundation of her choice. Through these initiatives, we hope to contribute to the visibility of her journey and the work she chooses to support. item.title: MPs ask what the break clause was for as Palantir wins two more years in the NHS
item.description: Lawmakers and campaign groups have slammed the UK government's decision to extend Palantir's controversial NHS contract by two years. Health minister James Frith told MPs on Monday that the current contract would continue until March 2029 as the government procures a new version of the Federated Data Platform (FDP). The existing Palantir-led deal , awarded in 2023, has a maximum value of £330 million and includes other suppliers. Frith said the new procurement would focus on interoperability, resilience, and trusted common standards in a "new FDP iteration" which would "welcome international and UK capability alike – whether that is UK small and medium-sized enterprises that want a crack at NHS contracts, sovereign AI-backed capability in the UK or any international provider worth merit." Palantir's cornerstone NHS contract win attracted criticism for lack of transparency. The US supplier had already won £60 million in NHS contracts without competition during and following the pandemic. Use cases from this period were carried over to the FDP. Critics have also challenged the evidence used to promote the FDP's claimed benefits . Dame Chi Onwurah, chair of the Commons Science and Technology Committee, said she was "extremely disappointed" by the decision. She challenged the government's reliance on continuity of care to justify keeping the contract, given its existing transition provisions. She said Palantir made it clear it would use the next two years to "embed itself even more deeply in our public services." "If a break clause cannot be exercised because of continuity of care, it is not a break clause; it is a lock-in. The Minister assured me that there were already contractual requirements that smooth continuity of care should continue. Were those assurances made in error?" she asked Frith. Frith confirmed that the contracts included exit and transition provisions and that migration was "possible in principle." "However, given the requirement for a new iteration, given performance and the benefits already in play, and given the opportunity to add new capability, including maternity services, to a next generation of FDP, an 18 to 24-month period for commission and procurement is a reasonable assessment," he said. Technology and government priorities had moved on since the original FDP procurement in 2023, he told MPs. "We will begin a new procurement process along different lines from the current contract," he said. The formal process is set to start during the second half of next year and take around 18 months. "Interoperability, resilience, and trusted common standards can and must be baked into the next generation of FDP. We will also start work, alongside the new procurement, with different providers on developing new capabilities and expertise starting with systems used in maternity care. item.title: 2027 Grammys: Tems, Angélique Kidjo, Burna Boy, Rocky Dawuni & More Lead African Nominees
item.description: Rocky Dawuni, Angélique Kidjo, and Burna Boy are among the African nominees at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards. If your timelines have been buzzing with celebration, hot takes, and group-chat debates since the 69th Annual Grammy Awards nominations dropped, you are definitely not alone. From record-breaking milestones to long-awaited solo albums and cross-continental collaborations, African nominees at the 2027 Grammys are having a massive moment across both the global and genre-specific categories—with Nigerian , Ghanaian, and Beninese stars leading the charge. Leading the headlines is Tems , who has officially made history as a 12-time Grammy nominee and the first Nigerian woman to earn four nominations in a single year. Already a two-time Grammy winner—having picked up Best Melodic Rap Performance in 2023 for her feature on Future’s “Wait for U” alongside Drake , and Best African Music Performance in 2025 for “Love Me JeJe”—she returns to the 69th Grammy Awards in four categories. Her acclaimed project Love Is a Kingdom is up for Best Global Music Album , while “Big Daddy” competes for Best African Music Performance, and “What You Need” earns double recognition in Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song. Right alongside her in the Best African Music Performance race is an exciting lineup of Nigerian, Ghanaian, and Beninese stars. Asake secures two nods in the category—for his solo song “Gratitude” and for “Jogodo” alongside Wizkid —bringing his career total to four Grammy nominations following his previous nods for “Amapiano” with Olamide in 2024 and “MMS” with Wizkid in 2025. For Wizkid, “Jogodo” marks his seventh career Grammy nomination, adding to a run that includes his 2021 Best Music Video win for “Brown Skin Girl” with Beyoncé , Blue Ivy Carter , and Saint Jhn . Ghanaian musicians King Ayisoba and Rocky Dawuni also join the Best African Music Performance lineup with their nomination for “No Tradition, No Africa”. Tems, Asake, and Ayra Starr lead the stellar lineup of African nominees contending for Best African Music Performance at the 69th Grammy Awards. Ayra Starr is celebrating a major milestone of her own, earning two nominations at the 69th Grammy Awards to bring her career total to four nods, following earlier Best African Music Performance recognition for “Rush” in 2024 and “Gimme Dat” in 2026. This cycle, she competes in Best Global Music Album for her album Starrgirl and teams up with five-time Grammy winner Angélique Kidjo in Best African Music Performance for “Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)”. Kidjo picks up three nominations in total this year, adding Best Global Music Album for Hope!! and Best Global Music Performance for “Bando [Orchestral]” featuring Pharrell Williams and Quavo. Angélique Kidjo and Ayra Starr sitting in a recording studio for their Aye Kan collaboration. item.title: PostgreSQL patches 52 security holes, sends version 14 into retirement
item.description: PostgreSQL developers have patched 52 security vulnerabilities and more than 140 bugs in updates spanning versions 14 to 18, alongside a second release candidate for version 19. The batch includes PostgreSQL 14.25, the final release for the now-unsupported version 14. Users are advised to move to a newer major version. Some fixes also require follow-up work, including rebuilding affected indexes or taking a fresh full backup. Administrators should check the release's post-update instructions. Alastair Turner, community technologist at open source consultancy Percona, said the high-severity code execution flaws should be taken seriously, although exploiting them requires database access. "This isn't something just a brute-force scan of the right port is going to find," he said. "They can make compromises through SQL injection or credential theft a lot worse, but don't create the opportunity for remote, anonymous code execution." Among the fixes is CVE-2026-6460 , a type confusion flaw that could let a database user with permission to create objects execute arbitrary code. It carries a CVSS severity score of 8.8 out of 10. Turner attributed the growing number of security discoveries partly to AI-assisted scanning and partly to increased scrutiny as PostgreSQL gains ground in enterprise computing. "It is a record number of CVEs fixed in a quarterly release, and I don't think we've seen the end of that trend. Looking down the list of where these CVEs came from, we see Anthropic and OpenAI open source scanners, so it is clear AI or brute force is playing a role," he said. Turner said the fixes spanned multiple parts of the software. There "isn't one piece of code that was broken" but rather "a wide base that got patched." "It's also worth noting that this is the third quarterly release in a row which sets a new record for the number of CVEs patched," he added. PostgreSQL 14 users now face a major-version upgrade or running without further security and bug fixes. Their destination may depend on internal upgrade policies. Organizations that require the previous major release, known as N-1, would currently target PostgreSQL 17, Turner noted. Version 18 remains the latest generally available release until 19 arrives. PostgreSQL 19 is scheduled for general availability on Thursday, November 19, barring further problems. It is set to include a new REPACK command , whose CONCURRENTLY option allows reads and writes to continue while disk space is reclaimed. VACUUM FULL requires an exclusive table lock, blocking reads and writes while it runs. ®

item.title: Are Nigerian Artists Dominating the Grammys’ Best African Music Performance Category?
item.description: Tems receiving the Best African Music Performance at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. A song should not earn a nomination simply because it is popular or has enjoyed international success. A closer look at the nominations across the four editions reveals just how much Nigerian music has featured in the category. In 2024, four of the five nominated recordings featured Nigerian artists. The following year, all five recordings had Nigerian representation, with seven Nigerian artists making the list. In 2026, three of the five recordings featured Nigerian artists, while the 2027 nominations saw four out of five recordings feature at least one Nigerian artist. Altogether, Nigerian artists have featured in 16 of the 20 nominated recordings since the category was introduced. This is not to suggest that Nigerian music does not deserve the recognition it receives. Nigerian artists have built impressive international careers, and their music has found audiences far beyond th

item.title: The future of datacenters depends on behind-the-meter energy generation
item.description: For the last decade, the datacenter industry has been a quiet engine of the digital economy. It was a background utility that just worked. However, datacenters are no longer passive consumers of electricity. They are becoming active participants in energy generation, storage, and grid management through behind-the-meter infrastructure. This is being driven by the explosive rise of AI and a manufacturing renaissance. Power demand is growing again, increasing an average of 2.1 percent annually over the past five years, with datacenters emerging as a dominant driver of long-term growth. Electric Power Research Institute projects that datacenters could consume as much as 17 percent of U.S. electricity by 2030 , more than triple their current 4-5 percent share. This massive spike in demand is clashing directly with a severely constrained power grid. Key regional utility transmission organizations are expected to face critical reserve shortfalls as early as 2028. At the end of 2025, more than 2,060 GW of new generation and storage capacity was represented by projects actively seeking interconnection to the U.S. grid. For the projects that successfully reached commercial operation, the process took a median of more than five years from request to completion. To keep building at the speed of innovation, datacenter operators are fundamentally rethinking their relationship with power , shifting from being passive grid consumers to active, localized energy producers. Grid capacity is no longer the ceiling. Instead, the next chapter of digital infrastructure will be written behind the meter. Behind-the-meter (BTM) refers to energy assets located on the customer side of the utility connection, including battery systems, microgrids, generators, fuel cells, and distributed energy resources that can operate independently of grid constraints. The Role of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) While every datacenter developer faces grid constraints, the industry’s two dominant business models are adopting distinctly different strategies to bypass the power bottleneck. Hyperscale Operators Hyperscale operators (tech giants like Amazon, Google, and Microsoft) utilize their massive balance sheets to secure gigawatt-scale capacity directly. Rather than acting as passive grid customers, hyperscalers are taking direct, active control of their energy supply chains. They negotiate custom, state-level tariffs directly with utilities, co-locate facilities next to large nuclear or baseload assets, and sign massive off-site Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs). Increasingly, hyperscalers are also deploying large-scale, on-site Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) to bypass grid delays and accelerate their projects. Many are also turning to behind-the-meter natural gas generation to provide additional power on-site. item.title: Japan's Fugaku supercomputer has decidedly un-super security
item.description: The RIKEN Center for Computational Science, the home of the Fugaku supercomputer, has revealed unauthorized attempts to access the machine after a data leak. According to a statement issued by RIKEN yesterday, between November 10 and 13 an unknown entity attacked a web dashboard that displays operational status data for Fugaku. It sounds like whatever the attackers did to that dashboard allowed them to move across the RIKEN network, because they were able to reach several servers that store data belonging to authorized users, and install malware. The servers stored users’ names and email addresses, plus credentials used to access supercomputers and services not operated by RIKEN. The attacker has tried to use those credentials. RIKEN is working with the organizations that host those other supercomputers to investigate whether the attackers succeeded. The research outfit doesn’t know how the attack happened and can’t say with certainty what information attackers were able to access and/or steal, beyond saying that 4,222 registered users of Fugaku are at risk, along with 375 registered users of its smaller Rikyu supercomputer. RIKEN does know that on November 13, someone attempted to log onto Fugaku. RIKEN quickly took the machine offline. Fugaku comprises 158,976 nodes, each packing a 48-core processor and 32GiB of available RAM, for a total of 7,630,848 cores and over five petabytes of memory. Those specs saw Fugaku lead the Top 500 lists of Earth’s mightiest supercomputers for two years between 2020 and 2022. It ranks ninth on the update of the list released on Tuesday. RIKEN’s other super, Rikyu, operates 288,000 cores. If attackers managed to run a workload on either machine, they could do a lot of damage. The intrusion has already had serious consequences because Fugaku is currently offline. As the machine is used for scientific research, and RIKEN schedules use of the machine, the outage will disrupt researchers who were waiting for their turn to use the supercomputer. At the time of writing, RIKEN has found no evidence that users’ research data has leaked but isn’t yet sure what info did make it out of the building and whether it contains any data describing third parties. The research org has promised to conduct a detailed investigation into the incident, which is the latest in a long string of significant cyberattacks that have struck Japanese clouds , telcos , retailers and government agencies, leading Tokyo to release emergency funds in the hope that extra money can quickly shore up the nation’s cyber-defenses. ®

item.title: 350 tech jobs hammered as TCS takes over work at iconic Australian retailer
item.description: Indian tech giant Tata Consultancy Services has a new client, iconic Australian retailer Bunnings Warehouse which has made a third of its IT department redundant. Bunnings is Australia’s equivalent of big box hardware retailers Home Depot and B&Q and earlier today advised its IT teams to attend a town hall meeting. The Register understands the invitation to that meeting was sent twice, after the first effort contained an error. We hear from staff that the botched invitation was taken as a clue of what was to happen next, namely the announcement of 230 redundancies plus an end to 120 contracted roles. The town hall meeting was not interactive, with a Bunnings rep speaking from a script and not taking questions. Staff whose roles will end then received an email inviting them to a meeting. Bunnings, whose logo is a hammer, has tried to explain the decision in a statement that says, “We need a technology model and partner that keeps pace with our customers so that we can continue to deliver the service, value and helpful advice people expect from us.” “These changes reflect the way customers are choosing to shop and the increasingly competitive retail environment,” the statement adds, before pointing out “Bunnings is already investing in technology and digital experiences to respond to these changes, earlier this year becoming the first Australian retailer to launch an AI-powered shopping agent using Google's Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience platform through Buddy.” Some of the TCS workers Bunnings is hiring will work in Australia. Others will work from India and the Philippines. While Bunnings follows the template of a big box retailer, each of its stores allows charities and community groups to run fundraising barbeques in its forecourt every weekend. Those barbeques are a significant source of income for many non-profits and have earned the chain a broad social license. The hardware barn is so well-known that children’s TV show Bluey – the most viewed program of 2024 and 2025 in the US – gently parodied it as "Hammerbarn" it in an episode. The Register mentions this because we understand the reference to TCS staff helping to deliver the Bunnings experience has gone down badly, as the chain’s employees wonder how offshore workers who have not experienced its stores and atmosphere can deliver a service that preserves its culture. Bunnings says its new IT operating model will commence in July 2027 and that “Impacted team members will be supported in their roles through Christmas, with any changes taking effect in the new year.” The company’s IT team will still employ around 500 people. These job losses add to a rotten year for Australia’s tech scene, which this year saw local heroes Canva and Atlassian farewell hundreds of staff. Iconic Australian airline Qantas last week outsourced hundreds of jobs to India through Accenture. ®

item.title: US extends chip sale restrictions to more Asian countries to reduce risk of ‘diversion’ to China
item.description: The US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has decided to ban remote access to certain GPUs and servers running in datacenters located in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. The agency has also introduced a requirement to secure a license before selling what it describes as “advanced super intelligence (SI) chips and servers” that are sufficiently powerful to “be used for training or running of advanced SI models” into the five nations. The interim final rule [PDF] containing the new regulations says they’re needed “to prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on US technology to threaten US national security and foreign policy interests.” Similar language can be found in previous US bans on sales of GPUs and other advanced tech to China, which Washington fears will use advanced tech to improve its military capabilities. US authorities understood that export bans wouldn’t prevent Chinese entities from renting GPUs housed elsewhere. So from 2021 to 2024, Washington introduced a series of regulations that required US-based clouds to make sure they didn’t serve Chinese customers. No such obligation existed for cloud operators elsewhere, which created a market for resources that Chinese customers could access from afar. It is widely felt that datacenter building booms in Malaysia and Thailand, both of which are generally on good terms with China, aimed to cater to Middle Kingdom customers who wanted to rent GPUs they could not import. Megapseed – whose former employee Alice Huang had an intimate relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and may have been a Chinese intelligence asset – built datacenters in Malaysia and was suspected of catering largely to offshore customers. Neil Shah, vice president of research at analyst firm Counterpoint, said the new rules shift the regulatory burden of complying with export controls from hardware manufacturers to cloud operators. “Data center operators in hubs such as Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia will now face massive ‘Know Your Customer's Workload’ requirements,” he told The Register by email, likening it to the KYC restrictions imposed on financial services firms. “They must prove to US regulators that their compute is not being funneled back to embargoed nations, or risk losing their own access to US silicon.” He feels the new rules represent “a severe short-term compute bottleneck for Chinese tech giants” and “a massive long-term catalyst for decoupling.” “Washington is forcing domestic capital and engineering talent to double down on full-stack sovereign alternatives, accelerating ecosystems like Huawei's Ascend.” Shah’s observation came days after Alibaba decided to spin out its T-Head chip design unit, which it described as “a leading provider of full-stack data center chips which enable system-level compute solutions in China.” That description suggests Alibaba doesn’t think T-Head has strong prospects of selling its

item.title: California sues OpenAI for misleading public about AI safety
item.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has sued OpenAI under the state's unfair competition and public nuisance laws, for allegedly misleading and endangering the public by deploying unsafe AI models. The lawsuit [PDF], filed in California Superior Court, follows the compromise of Hugging Face's infrastructure and other cyber incidents OpenAI's experimental models caused when taking autonomous actions without authorization or supervision. "While narratives about the Hugging Face attack have evoked science fiction fantasies of rogue AI systems run amok, let me be clear: the Hugging Face attack was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability — and this was only one of 80 known incidents," said Attorney General Bonta. At a press conference , Bonta added: "OpenAI disregarded public safety, knowingly tested potentially dangerous AI models without proper oversight and safety measures, and misled consumers and the public." The legal salvo comes after Bonta in September sent OpenAI a letter seeking information about these agentic attacks. According to the complaint, "OpenAI failed to substantially comply" with the investigatory subpoena. In August, 15 states led by Iowa – and excluding California – issued a joint demand for OpenAI to provide information about how its models hacked Hugging Face. OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment. Bonta's office previously joined with Delaware Attorney General Kathy Jennings to urge OpenAI to do more for children's safety in light of reports that its models produced sexually inappropriate output. California did not, however, join the eight states that sued OpenAI in October over alleged misrepresentations about child safety. Florida and Texas have also made child safety claims. Child safety plays well politically; California appears to be the first state to demand more accountability toward the general public. Bonta's lawsuit, in a state that has largely accommodated the AI industry for the sake of economic benefits and political contributions , suggests that California officials may be more willing to bite the hand that feeds. The many Democratic victories in the US midterm elections may also be a factor, as pundits feel voters swung to give lawmakers license to regulate the unpopular AI industry. At his press conference, Bonta made sure to convey that he wants accountability without smothering the AI industry in costly regulation. "Let me be clear," he said. "I believe in the technological and economic power of AI. If we're able to address these very high stakes safety issues, AI could lead to some of the most incredible improvements in the history of humankind." AI is yet to deliver those incredible improvements. It has delivered deepfakes, huge quantities of cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and the permissionless resale of past intellectual labor, plus high energy and RAM prices. item.title: Infoblox customer and staff data exposed in Sharepoint breach
item.description: Networking and security firm Infoblox is investigating a third-party breach that allowed crims to access sensitive customer and staff data. "Infoblox is investigating a security event involving unauthorized access to certain company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor,” a company spokesperson confirmed to The Register . According to sources, the compromised third-party data migration vendor had trusted access to Infoblox's SharePoint system, and the intruders used this vendor’s accounts and access to exfiltrate data directly from Microsoft SharePoint. This data included configuration information related to some customer's NIOS (Network Identity Operating System) deployments. These are saved snapshots of customers’ network data, such as DNS, DHCP configurations, Grid databases, and reporting logs, that can be used to fully recover the appliance or grid in case of a system failure or faulty upgrade. The intruders also stole employee data during the break-in. According to an email CEO Scott Harrell sent to employees, which The Register has seen, compromised employee details include financial information such as direct deposit details, contact info, dates of birth, and Social Security numbers for employees and dependents. Upon discovering the breach, Infoblox “immediately activated” its incident response procedures, and took steps to contain the incident, including hiring outside cybersecurity experts, the spokesperson said. “We have sent notifications about this security event and are providing support and guidance as appropriate,” the Infoblox spokesperson told us. “Based on our investigation to date, we have no indication that any Infoblox products, cloud services, software updates or build-and-release processes were involved. Our priority is to fully investigate and resolve this issue." Affected staff received a $100 "spot bonus" to buy password management services, and were warned to be "especially alert for phishing, vishing, fraud, or other suspicious communications." Infoblox also gave employees and their dependents free credit monitoring and identity protection for two years. Infoblox declined to answer our more detailed questions about the compromise, including the type of data exposed, and how many employees and customers might be affected. The Register will update this story as we learn more about the breach.®

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
item.description: null On Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials. They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster . The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA. It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there. (Image credit: SETI) Why it mattered The Arecibo message is only one of several messages intended for extraterrestrials, but this signal sent from Puerto Rico in 1974 was humanity's first intentional olive branch to the stars. At the time, it was the most powerful broadcast ever beamed into space, according to the SETI Institute. "The broadcast was particularly powerful because it used Arecibo's megawatt transmitter attached to its 305 meter antenna," SETI wrote of the broadcast in a project over. "The emission was equivalent to a 20 trillion watt omnidirectional broadcast, and would be detectable by a SETI experiment just about anywhere in the galaxy, assuming a receiving antenna similar in size to Arecibo's." The message was designed by astronomy professor Frank Drake of Cornell University (who also developed the famed Drake Equation for alien life), as well as Cornnell graduate students Richard Isaacman and Linda May, and Arecibo staff member James Walker, with input from astronomer Carl Sagan and others, according to Cornell University . The message included 1,679 bits that were arranged in 73 lines of 23 characters per line, all prime numbers, with the broadcast lasting less than 3 minutes, according to SETI. As of 2026, the message should have traveled about 52 light-years (1 light-year is the distance light travels in a year), with 24,948 light-years to go before reaching star cluster M13. The Arecibo message may have been the first message of its kind, but it wasn't the last. We have also included messages on several spacecraft, such as Pioneer and Voyager. NASA and Paul McCartney also b eamed a performance of "Across the Universe" in 2008. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Relive Starship's historic Flight 15 with our best photos from launch and 'Mechazilla' tower catch
item.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). The mission was billed as the first to bring both of Starship's stages, the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage, back to the launch site for recovery. And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase. It was the first-ever Ship catch, and a huge milestone toward SpaceX's ultimate goal: making Starship completely reusable. Liftoff occurred from Pad 2 at 5:47 p.m. EST (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local time) on Friday, against a near cloudless blue sky. Super Heavy is powered by 33 Raptor 3 engines, which provide more than 18 million pounds of thrust at liftoff. And lift off the booster did. The 33 Raptor engines of SpaceX's Starship V3 rocket during its test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) Starship roared off the pad under the power of those Raptors, pulsing visible shockwaves through the plume ejected from the rocket's flame trench. Starship climbs the sky above Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) The first couple minutes of flight went nominally; the vehicle climbed into the sky, gearing up for the hot-staging separation of Super Heavy and Ship — all of which was visible for miles, thanks to the clear Texas skies. Space.com's images taken from the media’s launch viewing area were shot on a Canon R5 Mark II , with an RF 200-800mm lens that made the sharp pictures of Starship’s liftoff and return possible from almost 4 miles away. EOS R5 Mark II: $3999 This mirrorless Canon has specs that make it one of the best cameras available right now, with impressive features and functionality, including a 45MP sensor and excellent high-ISO handling. Check our in-depth Canon R5 Mark II review . View Deal Starship climbs the sky above Starbase, Texas, as a bird passes on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) A successful separation occurred at T+2:21 minutes, as Starship soared approximately 40 miles (65 km) overhead. Once disconnected from its booster, Ship increased its thrust and continued onward to space , while Super Heavy, reoriented for its boostback burn and return to Starbase. Super Heavy (top) performs a boostback burn after stage separation as Ship 42 (bottom) fires its engines on its way to space. (Image credit: Space.com / Josh Dinner) That return, however, did not go entirely as planned. Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel alarm and autonomously shifted to an offshore splashdown rather than a catch attempt at Starbase. Super Heavy descends back toward Texas on Nov.

From Wande Coal reuniting with Juls and Patoranking linking up with Olamide for a musical salute to Lagos, to Khaid bridging generations with Fuji legend Saheed Osupa , Spyro delivering a quick dancefloor starter, and Seyi Shay trading English and French verses with Vegedream , there is plenty to keep your headphones busy over the next few days. Wande Coal – “Kowope” Kicking things off is Wande Coal , who reunites with British-Ghanaian producer Juls on “Kowope”, marking their first collaboration since the hit “So Mi So”. The new single is also Wande Coal’s first solo release since he put out his 15-track album KING COAL in June. This time, the pair lean into warm, percussion-led Afropop, with lyrics centred on wealth,celebration and abundance. Ahead of its release on 12 November 2026, Wande Coal gave fans a taste of what was coming with a video staged as an owambe celebration inside a banking hall—a fitting preview for a song that takes its cues from the festive side of Nigerian life. ﻿ Patoranking featuring Olamide – “Welcome to Lagos” Keeping that celebratory mood going, Patoranking and Olamide join forces on “Welcome to Lagos” to give Nigeria’s commercial capital its own musical tribute. The Afro-dancehall collaboration captures the city’s familiar mix of hustle,nightlife and everyday movement, with both artists bringing their distinct sounds to the record. Patoranking opens with his dancehall delivery, setting the pace before Olamide takes over with Yoruba verses rooted in the city’s street culture.Released on 10 November 2026 alongside an official music video, the track gives two of Nigerian music’s established names a chance to celebrate the city that continues to inspire countless songs. ﻿ Khaid featuring King Dr. Saheed Osupa – “Yasin” Switching lanes from contemporary street anthems to a meeting of two musical eras, Khaid takes an unexpected turn on “Yasin” alongside Fuji veteran King Dr. Saheed Osupa . The song brings Khaid’s contemporary Afrobeats melodies together with Osupa’s traditional Fuji vocals and talking-drum rhythms, giving both artists room to draw on their distinct musical styles. An official lyric video followed on 14 November 2026. With this collaboration, Khaid steps beyond the sound audiences may be most familiar with, while Osupa brings his unmistakable Fuji influence to a new musical setting. ﻿ Spyro – “Kpan Kpan” If you are looking to pick up the tempo even further, Spyro keeps things firmly on the dancefloor with “Kpan Kpan”, a two-minute, 19-second Afropop release produced by Colonel Tyemmy . item.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX’s Starship, already the largest rocket on Earth, will get even bigger with next-gen V4 model
item.description: null As usual, SpaceX and its founder Elon Musk are thinking big. The company recovered the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever on Saturday (Nov. 14), plucking it out of the sky with the "chopstick" arms of its Texas launch tower. It was a huge moment for SpaceX , bringing its vision of full and rapid rocket reuse much closer to reality. But Elon Musk isn't one to dwell on the past or rest on laurels, so he soon outlined an even more ambitious future for Starship. "Starship V4 will be ~70m [230 feet] long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load," Musk said via X, the social media platform he owns, on Sunday evening (Nov. 15). "Engine count will be raised to 9, with 3 more Raptor-Vacuum engines added, and these will be higher-thrust V4 engines." The current version of Starship — the one that launched Friday (Nov. 13) on the vehicle's 15th test flight — is the V3. It's the largest and most powerful rocket ever built, standing 408 feet (124 m) tall when fully stacked with its Super Heavy first stage and Ship upper stage. V3's Ship is 171 feet (52 m) tall and features six of SpaceX's Raptor V3 engines. (The similarly reusable Super Heavy V3 booster is powered by 33 Raptors.) So, as Musk noted in his post, the V4 Ship will be quite an upgrade in size and power. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk shared this chart depicting the evolution of SpaceX's Starship vehicles from the V2 to the planned V4 variant in August 2025. Exact specifications for Starship V4 are evolving. (Image credit: SpaceX/Elon Musk) Starship Die Cast Rocket Model Was $47.99 Now $39.99 on Amazon . Even if you can't see SpaceX's Starship in person, you can score a model of your own. Standing at 13.77 inches (35 cm), this is a 1:375 ratio of SpaceX's Starship as a desktop model. The materials here are alloy steel and it weighs just 225g. View Deal To provide a little perspective about that vehicle's planned dimensions: The V4 Ship will be the same height as a fully stacked Falcon 9 , SpaceX's workhorse two-stage rocket, and much broader: Ship is 30 feet (9 m) across, while the Falcon 9's payload fairing is 17.1 feet (5.2 m) wide. This isn't the first we've heard about a V4 Starship. Back in August 2025, for example, Musk posted a graphic showing Starship's planned progression from the V2 to the V3 to the V4, which he said is expected to debut in 2027. That slide pegs the future Starship's total height at 466 feet (142 m), 200 feet (61 m) of which would be Ship. But those numbers are out of date, Musk stressed in the post, saying that V4 is "probably closer to 150m height." So, yeah: If all goes according to plan, the next Starship will be nearly 500 feet tall. item.title: Attackers are using AI agents to automate cybercrime at 'industrial scale,' FBI and AWS warn
item.description: Attackers are using open source AI penetration testing framework ARTEX to automate their attacks on banks, governments, energy and healthcare providers, and other critical sectors around the globe, according to security alerts from the FBI and Amazon Threat Intelligence. Between October 3 and November 5, Amazon’s MadPot honeypot threat sensors detected two ARTEX campaigns: one that allowed thieves to steal AI credentials at “industrial scale” to gain free access to models, and a second that generated deepfake videos to trick live selfie checks. In the first one, miscreants used AI agents to steal API keys, and then feed these keys into the ARTEX framework’s model gateway to power more agents searching for more AI model access keys. “Agents validated identities through each provider’s token and identity services, enumerated storage, assessed permission scope, and went after managed AI model services, secrets and parameter stores, and application identities,” AWS Chief Information Security Officer CJ Moses wrote in a blog post on Friday. Targets included LLM gateways and proxy platforms such as One API, New API, Veloera, Sub2API, and LiteLLM, and AI application builders Dify, FastGPT, Langflow, RAGFlow, Open WebUI, LobeChat, and Ollama. This campaign also used cloud credentials to gain stolen access to the models. In a second campaign, attackers used ARTEX to create real-time deepfake videos to trick identity verification (KYC) checks at two cryptocurrency exchanges, and forged ID photos to pass document checks. “The agents reverse-engineered one vendor’s liveness protocol in detail, documenting the face-detection event stream it sends, how it tracks face position during the check, and the coordinate system it uses to tell the user where to move,” Moses wrote. The agents did manage to complete the full movement sequence with the face positioned within 7 pixels of the target, but this feat was not enough, as the vendor’s server-side verdict rejected the deepfake in every attempt. In a separate session, agents built a real-time deepfake video pipeline on a single consumer-grade GPU using an open-source face animation model. This video achieved 11.5 frames per second, which Moses said is “close to what a live video check expects.” Meanwhile, agents also worked on the ID document checks, building synthetic camera metadata whose image dimensions matched the real values inside the JPEG file, and preserving the original camera compression tables that are usually replaced by re-saving an edited image. While the end goal was stealing cryptocurrency, the campaign illustrates how ARTEX runs several sessions simultaneously, with multiple agents working toward the same result. “One searched for ways to cash out, one worked on clearing account balances, one set up the deepfake video pipeline, and one carried out the verification bypass,” Moses wrote. item.title: HTML-in-Canvas ships and could make the web a lot more creative...and a lot stupider
item.description: After two years of experimentation, the Chrome team shipped the HTML-in-Canvas API with Chrome 157. With it comes a new vision of how Web pages could be designed, for better or worse, allowing richer, more interactive elements but also more opportunities for annoying ads. “Previously, when creating visually demanding web apps, you had to choose between standard HTML elements and raw canvas contexts,” enthused one Google DevRel in a tutorial . “HTML-in-Canvas eliminates these trade-offs.” The Web API has been submitted for inclusion in the WHATWG HTML Living Standard , the ever-updating standard formerly known as HTML5 – for all the technologies that officially make up HTML (including Canvas itself). A Web API for the browser’s rendering engine Originally developed by Apple and standardized in 2014, the canvas tag is an HTML element that offers a space to render fluid graphics via JavaScript drawing commands. It creates a dedicated grid on screen, within which JavaScript can use a set of Canvas methods to draw lines, curves, text, gradients, and images. Or, the user’s GPU, via WebGL or WebGPU, can use the canvas to render 3D images and other custom effects. The downside of Canvas is that the regular HTML controls didn’t work inside the canvas itself. Formatting any text had to be done by hand. Interactivity was out, as were accessibility aids. Primarily developed by the Google Chromium team, HTML-in-Canvas allows JavaScript to place HTML commands within the canvas element, thanks to an attribute option within Canvas. If the canvas tag includes a content attribute of "drawable," the browser’s rendering engine prepares the HTML content inside the box so JavaScript can render it. While fully supported by Chrome and Chrome Android beginning with release 157, none of the other major browsers support the API yet (Microsoft Edge 157 – which is made of Chromium – unofficially appears to support at least some HTML-in-Canvas actions as well). The Web’s about to get lit Google posted a few possibilities of what can be done with HTML-in-Canvas. Developers can wrap HTML controls onto a 3D object. In one example , the user can turn the pages of a virtual book and even copy text out of the book itself. A video, complete with a set of controls , can be wrapped into an odd-sized canvas. The spec seems to work particularly well with JavaScript plug-ins, allowing coders to create entire 3D environments with Three.js , or to create charts with D3.js . Enthusiasts are already hacking against the spec with mad abandon. Developer Wes Bos put a notes app in the canvas , then used it as target practice by overlaying the app with some Duck Hunt-styled game code. HTML-in-Canvas “opens up the door to a lot of stupid use cases … but also a lot of really creative, interesting things where you can apply stylistic effects to HTML,” Bos explained on X . item.title: Tems Is Officially a 12-Time Grammy Nominee!
item.description: Tems is officially a 12-time Grammy nominee after securing four nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards. Photo Credit: Tems/Instagram One, two, three… and now 12! Tems has added four more Grammy nominations to her record, bringing her career total to 12 ahead of the 69th Grammy Awards. The latest recognition also makes her the first Nigerian female artist to receive four nominations in a single Grammy year, with this year’s shortlist recognising her work across four categories. The Nigerian singer is in contention for Best Global Music Album with her 10-track EP, Love Is a Kingdom , and Best African Music Performance for “ Big Daddy ”. She has also earned nominations for Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song for “ What You Need ”. The four nominations give her one of the most extensive Nigerian representations at this year’s ceremony and bring her Grammy wins to two, following previous victories in 2023 and 2025. Her relationship with the Recording Academy began in 2022, when she received her first nomination for her contribution to Wizkid ‘s “ Essence ”, which was nominated for Best Global Music Performance at the 64th Grammy Awards. The following year brought three more nominations, this time for her work on Future’s “ Wait for U ” featuring Drake and Beyoncé ‘s Renaissance . She won her first Grammy that night, taking home Best Melodic Rap Performance for “Wait for U”, while also receiving nominations for Album of the Year and Best Rap Song. Tems earned another nomination at the 66th Grammy Awards in 2024 for “ Lift Me Up ”, her contribution to the Black Panther : Wakanda Forever soundtrack, in the Best Song Written for Visual Media category. She returned to the Grammys the following year with three nominations, including Best Global Music Album for her debut album, Born in the Wild , and Best R&B Song for “ Burning ”. Her second Grammy win came in the Best African Music Performance category, where “ Love Me JeJe ” took home the award at the 67th Grammy Awards in February 2025. Now, with four nominations for the 69th edition, Tems has added another significant chapter to her Grammy record. The ceremony will take place on Sunday, 7 February 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. The post Tems Is Officially a 12-Time Grammy Nominee! appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

What exactly is a light-day? Here's what Voyager 1's latest milestone means for the interstellar probe
item.description: null After nearly 50 years traveling through space, NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is approaching a milestone no human-made object has reached before: a distance of one light-day from Earth. This milestone — which Voyager 1 is expected to reach on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (1016:07 GMT) — highlights the immense distances Voyager 1 has traveled and the challenges of communicating with spacecraft operating in the outer reaches of the solar system and beyond. Astronomers use a measurement known as a light-day to describe how far light travels in 24 hours. Light moves at approximately 186,000 miles (300,000 kilometers) per second, meaning one light-day is roughly 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers), according to a statement from NASA. Although the term light-day might sound like a measurement of time, it is actually a unit of distance, much like a light-year . Astronomers use light-based measurements because conventional miles and kilometers become increasingly difficult to comprehend when describing the enormous distances between objects in space. For perspective on how far Voyager 1 has travelled, sunlight takes about eight minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, meaning our planet is approximately 8.3 light-minutes from the sun. Radio signals traveling between Earth and Mars can take anywhere from three to 22 minutes, depending on the planets' positions in their orbits, according to the statement. By comparison, when Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth , a radio signal sent from the probe will take a full 24 hours to reach mission controllers on Earth, and a command transmitted from Earth will take another 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. A NASA visualization showing Voyager 1 looking back towards the solar system as it approaches one light-day away from Earth. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) The communication delay affects how engineers operate spacecraft at such distances. Unlike spacecraft operating closer to Earth, which can receive commands and return data with relatively little delay, communicating with Voyager 1 requires mission controllers to account for the extended signal travel time when planning spacecraft operations, troubleshooting technical issues and evaluating the results of commands sent to the probe. Voyager 1 has been traveling away from Earth since its launch on Sept. 5, 1977 . Now cruising through interstellar space at nearly 38,000 mph (61,000 kph), the spacecraft has spent more than 49 years covering the distance that light can cross in a single day. Even at that speed, Voyager 1 is moving relatively slowly compared with light itself. Its twin, Voyager 2 , which launched in 1977 on a different trajectory, is expected to reach the same one-light-day milestone in November 2035. As Voyager 1 and, eventually, Voyager 2 continue their journeys through interstellar space , their growing distances from Earth offer a measure of both the reach of human exploration and the communication challenges

item.title: 'Maybe the scariest thing I've heard in my life': Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover reveals his toughest challenge before flying to the moon
item.description: null TENERIFE, Canary Islands — Former NASA astronaut Victor Glover has flown in combat, performed four spacewalks and strapped himself to the top of rockets launching into space. But before embarking on his historic Artemis II journey around the moon, he faced something even more difficult: a conversation with his four daughters. Speaking alongside former astronaut Chris Hadfield at the Starmus VIII festival in Tenerife, Canary Islands, on Oct. 18, Glover opened up about the challenges of preparing his family for his riskiest mission yet. "This is maybe the greatest challenge of my astronaut career," Glover said. Glover joined NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Christina Koch and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen aboard NASA's Artemis II mission, which launched on April 1 , 2026, marking humanity's first crewed journey to the moon since Apollo 17 in 1972. But preparing for the historic journey wasn't just about mastering the spacecraft and executing the mission successfully. It also meant making sure his family was ready for what lay ahead. When Glover first traveled to space aboard SpaceX's Crew-1 mission in 2020, his children were much younger and he and his wife, Dionna, made a conscious effort to prepare them for his time in space. "We decided, as a parental unit, Dionna and I, that we were going to put as much effort into making sure our family was ready as NASA was putting into making sure I was ready to be a crew member," Glover explained. Victor Glover speaking at the Starmus VIII festival in Tenerife, Canary Islands, on Oct. 18, 2026. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic/Future) The family visited NASA's Kennedy Space Center , toured the launch pad and crew quarters and even planned when Glover would call home from the International Space Station . But by the time Artemis II came around, things were different. All four of his daughters were now adults, and preparing them for his journey around the moon meant discussing the mission's risks, including the possibility that he might not return home. Glover recalled his wife telling him something he described as maybe the scariest thing he'd ever heard. "You should have this talk with our daughters." And although he knew she was right, it wasn't an easy conversation to have. "We did, and it did not go well in my opinion," Glover admitted. "Well, it's not about going well. The talk needed to be done, just because it's hard." The following day, Glover sent his daughters and wife a poem, Live Your Life , by Chief Tecumseh. The poem helped Glover express something he had struggled to put into words during their conversation: why he believed the risks of traveling to the moon were worth taking. "It was a very tough conversation, but they understood that I know this is risky. I wasn't just telling them Dad's risking his life. There's a real point to this and there's a reason to take this risk," Glover explained. "This poem helped me to say it in a way that I didn't have words for." After trav
